objective_value: <float> Total cost of the solution, including all fixed vehicle costs, distance-based travel costs with the trailer towing surcharge where applicable, and handling costs for coupling and decoupling operations.

routes.vehicle_class: <int> Identifier of the vehicle class deployed on this route, specifying the truck type and whether a trailer is attached.
routes.vehicle_index: <int> Index distinguishing this deployed vehicle from other vehicles of the same class.
routes.customers_served: <list[int]> Identifiers of all customers visited and served on this route.
routes.route_sequence: <list[int], length variable> Ordered sequence of stop identifiers traversed on this route, in which each separate decoupling or coupling operation at a parking location is represented by its own distinct identifier so that repeated visits to the same parking location are distinguishable.
routes.route_sequence_physical: <list[int], length variable> Ordered sequence of physical location identifiers visited on this route, where the depot, customers, and parking locations are each referred to by their original location identifier.
routes.decouple_locations: <list[int]> Physical location identifiers at which the trailer is detached from the truck on this route.
routes.couple_locations: <list[int]> Physical location identifiers at which the trailer is reattached to the truck on this route.
routes.arrival_times: <dict, key: '{stop_identifier}'> Time at which the vehicle arrives at each stop along the route, where the key is the stop identifier from route_sequence and the value is the arrival time measured from the start of the planning horizon.

expanded_node_convention: Let n_orig be the number of physical locations and P be the instance parking-location IDs in their published list order. Physical nodes retain IDs 0..n_orig-1. The decouple copy of P[i] has ID n_orig+i, and the couple copy of P[i] has ID n_orig+len(P)+i. Both copies map back to physical location P[i].
